newsitem.title: UK: British policeman cleared of $2 calculator theft.
newsitem.headline: British policeman cleared of $2 calculator theft.

text.p: A British policeman was acquitted on Thursday of stealing a 1.5 pound ($2.38) calculator from his own station in a case that cost about 100,000 pounds ($158,800).
Andrew Whitfield, a 30-year-old officer from northern England, said he was only borrowing the calculator he was caught taking by a video camera in February 1995.
He has been suspended on full pay from his 21,000-pound ($33,340) job in north Yorkshire since the incident.
An earlier hearing in February ended in a mistrial. The jury on Thursday took just 65 minutes to return a not guilty verdict.
Estimates of the cost of trials, lawyers' fees, police investigations and Whitfield's salary have reached six figures.
